items.prompt: What happens to the speed of dissolving as the water gets warmer?
items.explanation: Warm water dissolves solids faster.

items.prompt: At what temperature does pure water boil?
items.explanation: Pure water boils at 100 °C.

items.prompt: A hot drink can dissolve ___ sugar than a cold drink.
items.explanation: Warmer water can usually dissolve more of a solid.

items.prompt: What is the difference between boiling and evaporation?

options.text: Boiling happens throughout the liquid at its boiling point, but evaporation happens at the surface at any temperature.

options.why: Evaporation can happen at any temperature.

hints: One happens at only one temperature.
Wet washing dries on a line.
items.explanation: Boiling occurs throughout the liquid at the boiling point. Evaporation is surface only and happens at any temperature.

items.prompt: Washing hangs on a line and dries on a cool, windy day. Is this boiling or evaporation?
items.explanation: The water leaves the surface of the clothes at a low temperature, so it is evaporation.

items.prompt: Bubbles rise through the whole of a pan of water on a stove. What is happening?

options.why: Evaporation happens at the surface only.

items.explanation: Bubbles forming throughout the liquid show that it is boiling.

items.prompt: Which has mass: an empty balloon or the same balloon full of air?

options.text: The full balloon has a little more mass.
The empty balloon has more mass.
options.why: The full balloon has the air too.

items.explanation: Air is a gas, and gases have mass, so the full balloon has more mass.

items.prompt: Sort each situation into boiling or evaporation.

items.text: bubbles form throughout a hot kettle
a puddle drying in the sun
wet hair drying in a breeze
a glass of water getting lower

hints: Boiling is at the boiling point.
items.explanation: Boiling needs the boiling point and bubbles throughout. Drying puddles and hair are evaporation.

items.prompt: Why does sugar dissolve faster in warm water than in cold water?

options.text: Warm water has more sugar in it.
The warm water particles move faster and mix with the sugar more quickly.

items.explanation: The faster-moving particles in warm water mix with the sugar particles more quickly.

items.prompt: A scientist adds sugar to 100 ml of cold water until no more dissolves, then warms the water. What probably happens?

options.why: Usually more can dissolve in warm water.

hints: The limit goes up with temperature.
items.explanation: Most solids dissolve more in warm water, so more sugar can dissolve.

items.prompt: A liquid boils at 78 °C. What does this tell you?
hints: Each pure substance has its own boiling point.
items.explanation: Pure water boils at 100 °C, so a liquid that boils at 78 °C is a different substance.

items.prompt: Why can a boiling point help us identify a substance?

options.why: Different substances boil at different temperatures.

options.text: Each pure substance boils at its own fixed temperature.
The boiling point is different every time.
options.why: It is fixed for a pure substance.

hints: Water and alcohol boil at different temperatures.
A pure substance has a set value.
We can compare to a table.
items.explanation: The boiling point is a property of a pure substance, so it can help us identify it.

items.prompt: Which statements about evaporation are true?

options.text: It can happen at temperatures below the boiling point.

options.why: It can happen at any temperature.

options.text: It makes bubbles throughout the liquid.
It happens at the surface of a liquid.

items.explanation: Evaporation happens at the surface and at any temperature.

items.prompt: Water vapour is water in the form of a ___.
items.explanation: Water vapour is water as a gas.

items.prompt: Why does a puddle disappear faster on a hot, windy day?

options.text: The wind makes the water boil.
Warmth and wind help more water particles escape from the surface.

items.explanation: Heat gives particles energy to escape, and wind carries the water vapour away.

items.prompt: A student heats a pan of water until it boils. The temperature stays at 100 °C. What is the best explanation?

options.text: The extra heat is used to change water into steam.
The water has stopped receiving heat.

hints: At the boiling point the temperature stays steady.
items.explanation: At the boiling point the extra heat changes water into steam, so the temperature stays at 100 °C.

items.prompt: Why does a hot drink cool down faster when you blow across it?

options.text: The air from your mouth is colder than ice.
options.why: Your breath is not that cold.

options.text: More water evaporates from the surface and takes heat away.

hints: The energy comes from the drink.
items.explanation: Evaporation takes energy from the drink, and blowing speeds it up.

items.prompt: A scientist tests four liquids. Liquid A boils at 100 °C, B at 78 °C, C at 118 °C and D at 56 °C. Which could be pure water?
items.explanation: Pure water boils at 100 °C, so liquid A could be water.

items.prompt: Liquid A boils at 100 °C and liquid B boils at 78 °C. How many degrees higher is the boiling point of liquid A?
hints: Subtract the smaller number from the larger.
items.explanation: 100 − 78 = 22. Liquid A boils 22 °C higher than liquid B.

items.prompt: A balloon full of gas and a similar empty balloon are placed on a balance. The full balloon is heavier. What does this show?

options.why: The full balloon is heavier because of the gas.

hints: The balloons are the same except for the gas.
items.explanation: The gas inside adds mass, so gases have mass.

items.prompt: True or false: Sugar usually dissolves faster in hot water than in cold water.
items.explanation: The particles in hot water move faster, so they mix with the sugar more quickly.

items.prompt: True or false: Boiling and evaporation are exactly the same thing.
hints: Boiling happens at the boiling point.
items.explanation: Evaporation happens only at the surface and at any temperature. Boiling happens throughout the liquid, with bubbles, only at the boiling point.

items.prompt: True or false: Pure water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
hints: What number is on the thermometer when bubbles rise?
It is the same as the freezing point plus 100.
It is the boiling point of water.
items.explanation: This is the boiling point of water. The temperature stays at 100 degrees Celsius while it boils, as the heat is used to turn it into vapour.

items.prompt: True or false: A solution is saturated when no more solid can dissolve in it at that temperature.
hints: What happens to extra sugar you keep adding?
Think of a spoonful that will not vanish.
items.explanation: Once the water holds as much dissolved solid as it can, any extra solid just sinks to the bottom. This is why a warm solution can usually hold more.
